grading_system.evidence: To graduate from Hartford High School, a student must earn a total of 26 credits and must meet all local and state graduation requirements ... In addition to the credit criteria, students must also demonstrate proficiency in certain, identified standards-based graduation requirements.
grading_system.proficiency_scale: Standards grading scale: E (Exceeds Expectations) 4.33, NE (Near Exceeds) 4.0, PR (Proficient) 3.0, NP (Near Proficient) 2.0, DP (Developing Proficiency) 1.0, BP (Beginning Progress) 0, NSE (Not Sufficient Evidence) 0 (GPA values, p.6)

schedule.evidence: The daily schedule is made up of four blocks of time, each consisting of 70 minutes. All students will be scheduled into an Advisory each day.

credit_definition.text: Credits are awarded per course. The catalog gives a credit value per course listing (for example 1 credit or .5 credit), but no explicit rule converting one-block semester courses or full-year courses to a credit count. A retaken course earns one credit, not two.
credit_definition.evidence: the student will receive one credit for the course (not two) and their grades will be averaged to determine their final grade for that course.

course_load.min_courses_or_credits: Grade 9 and 10: 8 credits (9 if in band/choir); Grade 11: 8 credits (9 if in band/choir; HACTC students 7); Grade 12: 8 credits (HACTC students 7)
course_load.evidence: Hartford High School students are required to take a minimum of the following credits: Grade 9 8 credits (9 credits if enrolled in band/choir)

local_grad_requirements.conversion_note: Catalog gives no conversion to standard credits (1 = full-year course), so total_in_credits is null. Distribution: English 4, Mathematics 3, Science 3 (includes a physical science and biology semester), Social Studies 3 (one must be US History), Fine Arts 1, Wellness 0.5, Physical Education 2, Required Courses 16.5, Elective Courses 9.5 (p.5). Recommended promotion credits: 6 for Grade 10, 12 for Grade 11, 19 for Grade 12 (p.5).

flexible_pathways_listed: Dual enrollment (Act 77, college courses; PLP required first)
Extended learning opportunities (ELOs) and community-based learning
Students may satisfy one required credit (English, Math, Science, Social Studies or Art) with certain two-year career/technical programs
Credit for courses taken abroad (international exchange, up to 8 credits per school year)
Regional Alternative Program (RAP) and Regional Resource Center (RRC)
notes: Current catalog is 2026-27 (headers are 2025-26 and 2026-27 text as printed). Graduation requires 26 credits plus identified standards-based proficiencies, culminating in a student-led conference in senior year (p.5). Student-level credit targets are 8 per year in grades 9-12 (p.5). Grading has two scales: an A-F alpha scale with GPA values, and a standards scale (E, NE, PR, NP, DP, BP, NSE) (p.6). Only AP courses are weighted (+1.00) (p.6). Daily schedule: four 70-minute blocks, plus Block 5 (flexible support) and Blocks 6-7 (placeholders) (p.6). Courses are listed as 'Fall / Spring' (semester, one block) or 'Full Year' (p.11-12 listings). Day-level course count is inferred as 4 from the four-block daily schedule; the catalog does not state courses per term directly. Students must complete a Personalizing Pathways half-credit course in grade 9 (p.5). Community service requirement is being reviewed; 2026 graduates need 5 hours (p.6). Some course listings are scrambled in the text layout, so the one-credit-per-course reading is not reliable and credit_per_course_term is left null.
